question.worked_solution:
The sum takes integer values of $a$ from $1$ to $3.$ So, computing the terms for $a=1,2,3$ and then adding them, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{a=1}^{3}a{(\frac{1}{2})}^{a+1} & =1{(\frac{1}{2})}^{1+1}+2{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2+1}+3{(\frac{1}{2})}^{3+1} \\  & =1{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+2{(\frac{1}{2})}^{3}+3{(\frac{1}{2})}^{4} \\  & =1\cdot \frac{1}{4}+2\cdot \frac{1}{8}+3\cdot \frac{1}{16} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{2}{8}+\frac{3}{16} \\  & =\frac{(1\cdot 4)+(2\cdot 2)+3}{16} \\  & =\frac{4+4+3}{16} \\  & =\frac{11}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
